name: Omara Ventures India
lm_rationale: Wealth Mine Networks — 4 SME IPOs in 2026 (₹138.86 Cr), 0% positive listings, 100% negative, −18.10% avg listing-day gain (chittorgarh 2026 SME tracker).
net_proceeds: ₹18.00 Cr to repay bank and FI borrowings, ₹10.00 Cr long-term working capital, ₹2.00 Cr to renovate and expand the Chandigarh boutique (first floor added) and ₹2.00 Cr for OMARA brand marketing, plus general corporate purposes.
key_risks: One Chandigarh boutique produced 82.92% of FY26 revenue, inventory of ₹43.58 Cr sits for about 347 days, and operating cash flow was negative in all three years (FY26 −₹6.70 Cr).
market_moat: Design-led natural-diamond jewellery sold under the OMARA brand with in-house design, customisation, BIS hallmarking and GIA-graded stones; gross margin rose to 39.58% in FY26.
management: Promoters Samarth Jaiswal and Ishani Mehta Jaiswal; 99.99% pre-issue promoter holding drops to 69.04% post-issue.
prose_business: Omara Ventures sells natural-diamond, solitaire and gold jewellery under the OMARA brand from a single boutique at Sector 9-C, Madhya Marg, Chandigarh. Designs are made in-house and manufactured by a product development and supply partner. Solitaire and diamond jewellery made up 66.96% of FY26 sales and gold jewellery 31.80%.
highlight_dev: The company has a landlord commitment (25 Jun 2026) for the first floor above its leased boutique and plans a ₹2.00 Cr renovation adding private client lounges and a bridal space, with a 60-90 day build.
sector_outlook: The RHP (citing IBEF) puts India's gems and jewellery market at ₹7,31,255 crore (US$85 bn) in January 2026, projected to reach ₹11,18,390 crore (US$130 bn) by 2030.
peer_sentence: At 14.48x post-issue FY26 earnings, Omara is below every peer in the RHP table: PNGS Reva Diamond Jewellery 18.05x, PN Gadgil Jewellers 20.75x, Advit Jewels 23.82x and BlueStone Jewellery and Lifestyle 763.27x. At 7.47x book it is richer than PNGS Reva (3.15x) and PN Gadgil (4.24x).
verdict_reason: 56% of proceeds repay debt; 7.47x book; LM 0/4 positive listings
why: FY26 revenue nearly doubled to ₹45.87 Cr and PAT jumped to ₹9.37 Cr (20.42% margin), but the business is one Chandigarh boutique and the FY26 jump includes a single Maharashtra customer worth 16.33% of sales. Cash is locked in ₹43.58 Cr of inventory and operating cash flow has been negative for three years, which is why ₹18.00 Cr of the ₹32.00 Cr stated objects goes to repaying loans. The 14.48x post-issue P/E looks cheap against listed jewellers, but 7.47x book is rich for a single-store retailer. Wealth Mine Networks has had all four of its 2026 SME listings open negative, averaging −18.10%.
suggestion: Avoid; growth is concentrated in one store and one year, and the lead manager's 2026 listings have all been negative.
